title: Migrate authentication secrets and redact derivative artifacts
description:
Stop storing Auth Builder credentials as plain text in request JSON, history, exports, logs, generated code, or previews. Model authentication separately from ordinary headers and store credential values in VS Code SecretStorage, leaving only stable secret references in persisted requests.

Migrate Bearer, Basic, and exact `X-API-Key` credentials conservatively from legacy data after creating a backup; never guess that arbitrary headers are secrets. Support Bearer, UTF-8 Basic, and API-key header/query placement with a documented conflict policy when a user also supplies the same header or query key. Resolve secrets only immediately before transport and use redacted templates everywhere else.

Exports and code generation remain redacted by default. Revealing or including credentials requires an explicit, contextual confirmation and must not leave secret material in history or diagnostics. Deleting/replacing auth removes obsolete SecretStorage entries. Tests must verify migration, redaction, conflicts, Unicode credentials, and cleanup.

checklist.text: Define AuthConfig and persisted secret-reference types separate from ordinary headers
Implement SecretStorage create, resolve, replace, and delete operations with no secret logging
Migrate only recognized Bearer, Basic, and exact X-API-Key legacy credentials after backup
Support UTF-8 Basic, Bearer, and API-key header/query injection with deterministic conflict handling
Use redacted placeholders in persistence, history, previews, diagnostics, exports, and generated snippets
Require explicit scoped confirmation before any export or code sample includes credentials
Remove orphaned secrets when auth changes or requests are deleted without affecting shared references
Add migration, Unicode, injection-conflict, redaction, confirmation, and cleanup regression tests
